findings.title: Confidence gate is still blocked by missing touched-module coverage evidence
evidence: pstf/features/SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP/confidence_report.json sets status to `needs_more_tests`, raw/final confidence to 0.85, and threshold to 0.90.
The same report scores `code_coverage` at 0.0 and records the explicit evidence gap: no Go or web coverage report exists under pstf/features/SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP/.
Repo tree for pstf/features/SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP contains no coverage/ directory or other coverage artifacts, so the release-evidence gap is real rather than stale bookkeeping.
findings.suggested_action: Generate touched-module Go and web coverage artifacts for the discovery/bootstrap slice, store them under the feature folder, and rerun confidence scoring before final human review.

findings.title: Operator settings still depend on a removed `systemInfo.nostr.relays` field with no replacement contract or regression proof
evidence: internal/api/handlers/system.go no longer populates `nostr.relays`, and the approved slice explicitly removed raw `nostr.relays` from the intended discovery contract.
web/src/routes/settings/+page.svelte:232-246 still renders `systemInfo.nostr.relays` as the operator-visible “Server Relays” setting.
A repo-wide test search found no settings-page or equivalent regression test covering the disappearance or replacement of that field after the discovery cleanup.

HITL-SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP-001 decided that raw `nostr.relays` should be fixed/removed from the bootstrap contract, but did not decide whether operator-facing relay visibility should still exist through another field.
findings.suggested_action: Decide whether operator-visible backend relay configuration should remain available after the sidecar-first cleanup. Then either add an explicit non-goal plus UI cleanup, or add a replacement contract and regression coverage for the settings surface.

proposed_hitl_question.question: After removing raw `nostr.relays` from the approved system discovery contract, how should the operator settings page handle server relay visibility?
options: Expose backend relay configuration through a new explicit operator-only field and test it
Remove server relay visibility from the settings UI and treat it as out of scope for this release
Keep current settings behavior by restoring `nostr.relays` for operator surfaces only
Defer the settings-page decision into a dedicated follow-up slice before release

findings.title: Several PSTF artifacts still describe superseded behavior, which weakens traceability for human review
evidence: pstf/features/SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP/feature_spec.json still says the handler exposes `nostr.relays` when the sidecar is disabled and that the browser helper falls back to that field, even though the implementation and verification artifacts say this was fixed.
The same feature_spec.json still lists a missing multi-consumer contract test in `contradictions_and_gaps`, but verification_report.md and test_matrix.json now mark SDRB-T-011 as passing.
pstf/features/SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP/test_matrix.json marks SDRB-T-012 as `pass`, but its title/description/preconditions still describe it as a blocked manual gate waiting on `bahia-u6e1`.
pstf/features/SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP/hitl_decisions.md metadata still says `Current Stage: acceptance_criteria`, which no longer matches the feature’s verification/confidence state.
findings.suggested_action: Refresh the stale feature spec, test-matrix text, and HITL metadata before final human review so reviewers do not have to reconcile obsolete statements against the live verification outcome.
